overall_reason: A model's default dashboard screen: indigo-to-violet gradient banner with "📊 Analytics Dashboard" and "updated in real-time 🚀", four equal emoji-labelled KPI cards with round invented numbers, and a settings card that contradicts itself; nothing on it belongs to any product or user.

findings.evidence: Failed T-DEFAULT-AGENT: "dashboard for a SaaS" yields exactly this: gradient hero banner (#6366f1 to violet), a row of four equal white cards with radius 8 and shadow 0 4px 6px, emoji + grey label + big number + grey delta in each, then one settings card. Adds the gradient banner and emoji labels to the sweep's saas-card-kit cluster.
findings.before: gradient banner + 4 emoji KPI cards + settings card
findings.after: Drop the banner (a page title in body ink is enough); give the KPI row one primary metric with a trend line and period, the rest as a compact table
findings.why: Every part is the stock answer; nothing reflects what this product measures or who uses it.

findings.evidence: T-FILLER: "$48.2k", "3,910", "1.8%", "62" with deltas "↑ 12%", "↑ 4%", "↓ 2%", "↑ 7% from last month" and no period, source or empty/loading state. The header promises "updated in real-time" while every delta is month-over-month.
findings.after: Bind to real data with an as-of timestamp, and design the empty and loading states (INT-159); in a mock, mark figures as sample data
findings.why: A dashboard is the place figures must be true; round invented KPIs with confident deltas are fake data presented as state.

findings.evidence: Sub-line says "changes are saved automatically" directly above a "Save Changes" button. One of the two is false.
findings.before: "Manage your account preferences — changes are saved automatically" + [Save Changes]
findings.after: Pick one model: autosave with a visible "Saved" trace (CMP-147) and no button, or an explicit Save with no autosave claim
findings.why: Contradictory save copy is the mark of text and UI generated separately; users cannot tell whether their change persisted.

findings.evidence: "Delete Account" sits 4px from "Save Changes", filled in the same brand indigo, in an unstyled browser-default bevel with a 21px target, plus a 🗑️ emoji button beside the email field that deletes something unnamed.
findings.before: [Save Changes][Delete Account] side by side, both indigo
findings.after: Move "Delete account" to a separate danger zone below, styled as a secondary/outline red control (CMP-122), with an undo or typed confirmation
findings.why: A destructive action styled and placed like the primary action is the opposite of a decision; the half-styled button shows nobody looked.

findings.where: h1, sub-line, KPI labels, field actions
findings.evidence: Seven emoji used as decoration or icons beyond the sweep's three counted: "📊" h1 prefix, "🚀" on the sub-line, "💰 👥 📉 ⭐" on labels, "✏️ 🗑️" as action buttons. T-DELETION: removing all of them loses nothing (the pencil on a field that is already an editable input means nothing).
findings.after: Remove the emoji; use a labelled text button ("Change email") or a proper icon set with accessible names
findings.why: Emoji as icons and as tone markers are among the strongest generated-UI tells.

findings.evidence: Value "user@example.com" shown as the account email.
findings.after: Bind to the signed-in user's email; in a mock, use an obviously sample address
findings.why: Placeholder identity in an account screen reads as unfinished.

not_investigated: No brief or product context; T-RIVAL-NAME and T-STOCK-ORDER have no category beyond 'generic dashboard' (no finding beyond T-DEFAULT-AGENT).
Nothing on the screen is specific enough to list as a strength.
